subject: Aurelia Health request: EU-only hard-pin for model + no-fallback

Subject: Aurelia Health request: EU-only hard-pin for model + no-fallback

Team — quick heads-up and request for feasibility/risks. Aurelia Health (contact: Samantha) is asking for a strict EU-only binding for their model calls plus an explicit "no-fallback" policy: they want requests pinned to a specific vetted model in eu-west-1 and no automatic fallback to other variants or regions under any outage scenario.

Why: regulatory counsel at Aurelia says certain PHI-derived flows must never cross region or be served by variants that are not on our approved quantization/profile. They're offering to pay for reserved capacity and sign an addendum (DPA + runbook) but procurement wants confirmation we can operationalize this without unacceptable risk.

Asks:
- Is hard-pinning a single model in a single EU region technically feasible today (routing + enforcement)?
- If feasible, what are the production risks (SLO impact, single-region failure modes, mitigations)?
- Can we enforce a true no-fallback policy (i.e., no auto-route to compatible model or region) while still meeting our reliability standards?
- What additional audit/logging/KMS controls would you require to sign off?

I appreciate quick POVs so I can respond to Samantha and let procurement know lead time and cost delta.

Thanks — Ethan
Ethan Park

Subject: Re: Aurelia Health request: EU-only hard-pin for model + no-fallback

Ethan — thanks for flagging. Short answer: we can implement a hard-pin and disable cross-region fallback, but there are tradeoffs I'll outline below.

Notes/concerns:
- Feasibility: yes. Our routing layer supports region pinning per-customer and model-variant pinning per-route. Enforcing a no-fallback policy is feasible by marking the route as \"strict\" and rejecting requests that can't be satisfied in that region/variant.
- Reliability: this will mean the customer's availability is tied to that region and that model. If the node pool for that model in eu-west-1 is degraded (kernel issues, capacity loss), requests will fail rather than be routed to a fallback. That could be unacceptable for some SLA classes.
- Ops burden: we'd recommend a dedicated capacity reservation for this customer to reduce the risk of transient capacity failures. Autoscaling and burst policies can be constrained to the reservation.
- Alternatives: 1) strict-region + same-region fallback to a quantized compatible variant; 2) strict-region + must-accept best-effort degraded mode (throttled/queued). Those give better uptime while keeping data residency.

For sign-off we'll need: a written customer acceptance of an outage policy (what we will/won't fallback to), a SOC2/PII handling addendum, and a runbook for incident response. If procurement has a standard DPA we can review it in parallel.

I'll coordinate with infra on exact implementation steps if we get buy-in.

- Lauren
Product Lead, Routing & Policies
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Bryce <samantha.bryce@aureliahealth.com>, procurement@aureliahealth.com
Date: 2028-04-05T11:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Aurelia Health request: EU-only hard-pin for model + no-fallback

Looping in security POV. We can accommodate this, but only with guardrails. High-level requirements we will insist on before we approve: 

1) Dedicated bounded capacity + HSM-backed KMS for keys used in that customer's workload (audit trail).
2) Extended retention for audit logs (token-level and routing decisions) for 1 year for auditability.
3) Pre-approved runbook and a contact for escalation (Aurelia must accept response windows and a defined maintenance window).
4) Signed DPA that includes language about accepted outage modes (if we refuse fallback, specify that outages are customer's risk unless we have a reserved fallback agreement).

I've attached a short rationale template you can share with Aurelia which explains what we can and can't do technically (Aurelia_Security_Rationale.pdf). It clarifies the difference between hard-pin and best-effort region-only.

From a platform risk perspective: hard-pin + no-fallback increases blast radius for that customer (their availability is dependent on a single region's operational health). We can mitigate but not eliminate that risk. Also note some kernel-level patches on our GPU fleet have required reboots; with no-fallback we need maintenance coordination.

I'll follow up with a checklist for infra changes.

—Rishi
Head of Security & Compliance
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Aurelia Health request: EU-only hard-pin for model + no-fallback

Thanks, everyone — appreciate the quick responses. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Aurelia is prepared to accept the availability tradeoff — our legal/regulatory team requires region and model immutability for the specified flows.
- We'll take the dedicated reserved capacity option and are fine with an explicit outage acceptance clause in the DPA.
- Procurement will send the DPA and a DocuSign for the capacity commitment by end of day; you'll see it from procurement@aureliahealth.com.
- We also request that audit logs and routing decisions for those flows be retained for 12 months and exported to a secure S3 bucket we control (or made available via an audited access path).

Can we get a short project timeline (engineering effort + expected lead time) and an initial cost estimate? We'd like to schedule a kickoff next week if possible.

Regards,
Samantha Bryce
Sr. Director, Product Compliance — Aurelia Health

2) Security (Rishi): needs DPA + reserved capacity + extended audit retention and KMS controls. Aurelia's request for 12-month log retention is noted and required for approval.
3) Commercial: Aurelia will send DocuSign for reserved capacity and a DPA; Ethan to review procurement doc and loop legal if needed.

Action items:

- Lauren: create an infra ticket and estimated timeline + rollout plan (canary, cutover, rollback criteria). Please include estimated SW + infra hours and lead time for reserved pool. (ETA: EOD 4/7)

- Marissa: coordinate an intro call with Aurelia's cloud ops & procurement; propose Wednesday 4/10.

Samantha — thanks for the clarity. We'll target a small technical kickoff next week and get an estimate in the EOD 4/7 timeframe. If procurement sends the DocuSign today we can start parallel legal review.
